180: function assertMutationOrigin(environment: AuthEnvironment, request: Request) {

191:     } catch (error) {
192:       if (error instanceof M1Error) throw error;
193:       throw new M1Error(403);
194:     }

1: import { getTreaty } from "../routes/api.$";
2: import type {
3:   BootstrapCompleteBody,
4:   BootstrapTokenBody,
5:   InvitationAcceptBody,
6:   InvitationCreateBody,
7: } from "../server/m1/models";
8: 
9: export type {
10:   BootstrapComplete,
11:   BootstrapReservation,
12:   InvitationAccepted,
13:   InvitationCreated,
14:   InvitationPublic,
15: } from "../server/m1/models";
16: 
17: export class M1ClientError extends Error {
18:   constructor(
19:     message: string,
20:     readonly status: number,
21:   ) {
22:     super(message);
23:     this.name = "M1ClientError";
24:   }
25: }
26: 
27: export async function m1Fetch<T>(path: string, init: RequestInit = {}) {
28:   const headers = new Headers(init.headers);
29:   if (init.body && !headers.has("content-type")) {
30:     headers.set("content-type", "application/json");
31:   }
32: 
33:   const response = await fetch(`/api${path}`, {
34:     ...init,
35:     headers,
36:   });
37:   const body = (await response.json().catch(() => null)) as { error?: string } | T | null;
38: 
39:   if (!response.ok) {
40:     throw new M1ClientError(readErrorMessage(body), response.status);
41:   }
42: 
43:   return body as T;
44: }
45: 
46: export async function reserveBootstrap(body: BootstrapTokenBody) {
47:   return unwrapTreatyResponse(await getTreaty().setup.reserve.post(body));
48: }
49: 
50: export async function completeBootstrap(body: BootstrapCompleteBody) {
51:   return unwrapTreatyResponse(await getTreaty().setup.complete.post(body));
52: }
53: 
54: export async function createInvitation(body: InvitationCreateBody) {
55:   return unwrapTreatyResponse(await getTreaty().invitations.post(body));
56: }
57: 
58: export async function getInvitation(token: string) {
59:   return unwrapTreatyResponse(await getTreaty().invitations({ token }).get());
60: }
61: 
62: export async function acceptInvitation(token: string, body: InvitationAcceptBody) {
63:   return unwrapTreatyResponse(await getTreaty().invitations({ token }).accept.post(body));
64: }
65: 
66: function unwrapTreatyResponse<T>(result: { data: T | null; error: unknown; status: number }) {
67:   if (result.error) {
68:     const value =
69:       result.error && typeof result.error === "object" && "value" in result.error
70:         ? result.error.value
71:         : result.error;
72:     throw new M1ClientError(readErrorMessage(value), result.status);
73:   }
74: 
75:   if (result.data === null) {
76:     throw new M1ClientError("The request could not be completed.", result.status);
77:   }
78: 
79:   return result.data;
80: }
81: 
82: function readErrorMessage(value: unknown) {
83:   if (value && typeof value === "object" && "error" in value && typeof value.error === "string") {
84:     return value.error;
85:   }
86: 
87:   return "The request could not be completed.";
88: }
89: 
90: export function safeRedirect(value: string | undefined, fallback = "/") {
91:   if (!value || !value.startsWith("/") || value.startsWith("//")) return fallback;
92:   return value;
93: }
94: 
95: export function formatClientError(error: unknown) {
96:   if (error instanceof M1ClientError && error.status === 429) {
97:     return "Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.";
98:   }
99: 
100:   if (error instanceof Error && error.message) return error.message;
101:   return "The request could not be completed.";
102: }

1: # Shui Roadmap
2: 
3: Last updated: 2026-08-14
4: 
5: ## Goal
6: 
7: Shui is a central identity platform that manages who can use each Application and which roles they have there. It communicates that state to Applications through OIDC/OAuth 2.1 and outbound SCIM 2.0 provisioning.
8: 
9: ```text
10: Identity Platform
11: ├── Principals
12: │   ├── Users
13: │   └── Service Accounts
14: ├── Teams
15: ├── System Roles
16: └── Applications
17:     ├── OAuth Resources
18:     ├── OIDC Clients
19:     ├── Assignments
20:     ├── Application Roles
21:     ├── Role Grants
22:     └── Provisioning
23: ```
24: 
25: ## Scope
26: 
27: ### Included
28: 
29: - Better Auth based human authentication and sessions
30: - OAuth 2.1 Provider with OIDC compatibility
31: - First-run setup that creates exactly one initial `root` User
32: - Invite-only User registration after setup
33: - Human Users and non-human Service Accounts
34: - Service Account credentials using the OAuth `client_credentials` grant
35: - User and Team ownership for Applications and Service Accounts
36: - System Roles for operating Shui
37: - Flat Teams containing Users
38: - Application Assignments independent from Application Roles
39: - Direct User and Service Account Application Role grants
40: - Team Application Role grants inherited by Team members
41: - Application-specific OIDC claims
42: - Outbound SCIM 2.0 provisioning with retries and reconciliation
43: - Responsive login, setup, invitation, consent, and administration UI
44: - Audit logging for security-sensitive and administrative operations
45: 
46: ### Not Included
47: 
48: - OAuth providers exposed by downstream Applications
49: - OAuth clients owned and managed inside downstream Applications
50: - Application-specific permissions such as `repo:write`
51: - Access tokens issued by downstream Applications
52: - Nested Teams or Team DAGs
53: - Deny roles or deny grants
54: - General-purpose policy language
55: - Inbound SCIM into Shui
56: 
57: ## Fixed Decisions
58: 
59: - Runtime and deployment: one Cloudflare Worker with a custom module entrypoint
60: - Web framework: TanStack Start with React 19
61: - API framework: Elysia mounted inside a TanStack Start server route under `/api/*`
62: - Elysia integration: dispatch standard `Request` objects through `app.fetch(request)` instead of exporting Elysia's experimental Cloudflare adapter directly
63: - Typed API client: Eden Treaty, using direct in-process calls during SSR and HTTP in the browser
64: - Database: Cloudflare D1 with Drizzle ORM
65: - Build and frontend delivery: Vite, `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`, and Workers Static Assets
66: - UI: Kumo UI with Tailwind CSS v4
67: - Forms and server state: TanStack Form and TanStack Query
68: - API validation: Elysia `t` / TypeBox
69: - Formatting and linting: Vite+ with Oxlint, Oxfmt, and TypeScript strict mode
70: - Async provisioning: Cloudflare Queues with a dead-letter queue
71: - Authentication: Better Auth
72: - Provider: `@better-auth/oauth-provider`, not the legacy `oidcProvider`
73: - Better Auth version: pin all Better Auth packages to `1.7.0-rc.5`
74: - Teams remain separate from Principals; Principals are Users and Service Accounts
75: - Application Assignment and Application Role Grant are separate records
76: - Team Assignment is inherited by Team members
77: - Team Role Grants are inherited by Team members
78: - A Role Grant never creates an Assignment implicitly
79: - Roles are effective only while the subject has an effective Assignment
80: - Direct and Team-derived Role origins remain distinguishable
81: - Service Account credentials are OAuth Clients, not a second custom API-key system
82: - One Service Account can have multiple OAuth Client credentials for safe rotation
83: - Better Auth owns authentication protocol data; Shui owns authorization and provisioning data
84: - Better Auth Organization roles are not used as Shui System or Application Roles
85: - Better Auth SCIM plugin is not used because it provides inbound SCIM, while Shui needs outbound provisioning
86: - TanStack Start Server Functions do not contain domain business logic; domain reads and mutations go through Elysia services and routes
87: 
88: ## System Architecture
89: 
90: ```text
91: Browser
92:   │ HTTPS
93:   ▼
94: Single Cloudflare Worker
95:   ├── fetch
96:   │   └── TanStack Start
97:   │       ├── React 19 SSR and routing
98:   │       ├── Workers Static Assets
99:   │       └── /api/* -> Elysia app.fetch(request)
100:   │                    ├── Better Auth handler
101:   │                    │   ├── Email/password authentication
102:   │                    │   ├── Sessions
103:   │                    │   ├── OAuth 2.1 / OIDC Provider
104:   │                    │   └── JWT / JWKS
105:   │                    ├── Identity and authorization services
106:   │                    └── Audit and outbox writer
107:   ├── queue -> provisioning consumer
108:   └── scheduled -> outbox dispatch and reconciliation
109:        │
110:        ├── D1 via Drizzle
111:        ├── Cloudflare Queues
112:        └── Application SCIM endpoints
113: ```
114: 
115: Elysia's direct Cloudflare Worker adapter is currently experimental, so Shui does not export it as the Worker entrypoint. Elysia runs through its documented TanStack Start integration and receives requests through `app.fetch(request)`. This combined path must still be tested in the actual Workers runtime rather than only in Node.js. The custom Worker entrypoint delegates `fetch` to TanStack Start and also exposes `queue` and `scheduled` handlers.
116: 
117: ## Domain Semantics
118: 
119: ### Principals
120: 
121: `User` represents a human and maps one-to-one to a Better Auth User. `Service Account` represents a Bot, CI job, or backend process and never receives a fake email/password User.
122: 
123: Principal IDs are stable and never reused. Disabling a Principal immediately prevents new token issuance. Existing JWTs remain valid until expiration, so access-token lifetimes must stay short.
124: 
125: ### Teams
126: 
127: Teams contain Users only. Service Accounts cannot become Team members in the initial scope. Teams are flat and cannot contain other Teams.
128: 
129: Teams may own Applications and Service Accounts. Ownership identifies the responsible party but does not implicitly grant an Assignment, Application Role, or System Role.
130: 
131: ### System Roles
132: 
133: Initial built-in System Roles:
134: 
135: | Role | Purpose |
136: | --- | --- |
137: | `root` | Full control of Shui and recovery-critical operations |
138: | `user-admin` | Manage Users, invitations, Teams, and memberships |
139: | `application-admin` | Manage Applications, Assignments, Roles, OIDC Clients, and provisioning |
140: 
141: System Role definitions and permission mappings are code-defined initially. Grants are stored in D1. Application Roles remain dynamic and Application-specific.
142: 
143: The last active `root` User cannot be disabled, deleted, or stripped of `root`.
144: 
145: ### Applications
146: 
147: An Application is a service that trusts Shui. Each Application has:
148: 
149: - One OAuth Resource identifier used as the Access Token audience
150: - One or more OIDC/OAuth Clients
151: - Independent Assignments for Users, Service Accounts, and Teams
152: - Dynamic Application Roles
153: - Direct and Team Role Grants
154: - Optional outbound provisioning configuration
155: - An owner that is either a User or Team
156: 
157: Human-facing OIDC Clients and Service Account credentials are both OAuth Clients, but their purposes are recorded separately and validated differently.
158: 
159: ### Assignments
160: 
161: Assignment controls whether a subject may use an Application and whether it is included in provisioning.
162: 
163: ```text
164: effective User Assignment
165: = direct User Assignment
166:   OR active Assignment of any Team containing the User
167: 
168: effective Service Account Assignment
169: = direct Service Account Assignment
170: ```
171: 
172: The following states are intentionally different:
173: 
174: | State | Login/token issuance | Provisioning | Roles |
175: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
176: | Not assigned | Denied | Deprovisioned | Not effective |
177: | Assigned without Roles | Allowed | Active | Empty list |
178: | Assigned with Roles | Allowed | Active | Effective Role list |
179: 
180: ### Application Roles
181: 
182: Application Roles describe what a Principal is inside one Application. They do not define concrete permissions inside Shui or the downstream Application.
183: 
184: ```text
185: effective User Roles
186: = direct User Role Grants
187:   UNION Team Role Grants from all active Team memberships
188: 
189: effective Service Account Roles
190: = direct Service Account Role Grants
191: ```
192: 
193: Effective Role evaluation occurs only after an effective Assignment is confirmed. Duplicate Role keys are removed for claims, while all Direct and Team origins are retained for administration and audit responses.
194: 
195: Removing one origin does not remove a Role when another origin still grants it.
196: 
197: ### Service Account Credentials
198: 
199: Each Service Account credential is a confidential OAuth Client that supports `client_credentials` and is linked to exactly one Service Account and one Application Resource.
200: 
201: The OAuth Client's `client_id` and `client_secret` are the credential. The secret is displayed once and stored only in the secure form provided by Better Auth.
202: 
203: Credential rotation uses overlap rather than in-place secret rotation:
204: 
205: 1. Create a new OAuth Client credential.
206: 2. Link it to the same Service Account and Application Resource.
207: 3. Move the consumer to the new credential.
208: 4. Disable and later delete the old OAuth Client.
209: 
210: This avoids downtime because Better Auth's in-place rotation immediately invalidates the old secret.
211: 
212: ## OIDC And OAuth Contract
213: 
214: ### Flows
215: 
216: - Human login: Authorization Code Flow with PKCE S256
217: - Service Account: Client Credentials Grant
218: - Refresh Token Grant: disabled for the initial release
219: - Dynamic Client Registration: disabled
220: - Unauthenticated Client Registration: disabled
221: - JWT Access Tokens: required for downstream Applications
222: - Opaque Access Tokens: not accepted by downstream Applications
223: 
224: Refresh tokens remain disabled until Better Auth 1.7 is stable or D1 concurrency testing proves refresh-family rotation and invalidation safe.
225: 
226: ### Audience Rules
227: 
228: - Access Token `aud`: the target Application's OAuth Resource identifier
229: - ID Token `aud`: the authenticating OIDC `client_id`, as required by OIDC
230: - `iss`: Shui's canonical public issuer URL
231: - `azp` / `client_id`: the authenticated OAuth Client
232: 
233: Clients must be linked to allowed Resources. Managed Clients request exactly one Application Resource per flow. Tokens requesting no Resource, an unknown Resource, multiple Resources, or a Resource owned by another Application are rejected.
234: 
235: ### Claims
236: 
237: Standard OIDC claims are exposed according to scopes through ID Token and UserInfo behavior supported by Better Auth:
238: 
239: - `sub`
240: - `name`
241: - `email`
242: - `email_verified`
243: 
244: Shui-specific claims use a URI namespace based on the final issuer domain:
245: 
246: - `application_id`
247: - `principal_id`
248: - `principal_type`
249: - `roles`
250: - `teams`
251: - `authz_version`
252: 
253: Only data for the target Application is included. System Roles and Roles belonging to other Applications must never appear.
254: 
255: For human flows, `sub` identifies the User according to the Provider's subject policy. For `client_credentials`, `sub` identifies the OAuth Client credential. Applications use the namespaced `principal_id` claim when they need the stable Service Account identity across credential rotation.
256: 
257: Team claims contain only Teams relevant to the target Application. Claim keys and shape are versioned before the first production release.
258: 
259: ## Data Model Direction
260: 
261: Better Auth generated tables remain isolated as authentication infrastructure. Domain migrations reference Better Auth Users but do not modify generated tables manually unless required by a documented plugin extension.
262: 
263: Core Shui tables:
264: 
265: - `principals`
266: - `human_principals`
267: - `service_accounts`
268: - `teams`
269: - `team_memberships`
270: - `system_roles`
271: - `system_role_grants`
272: - `applications`
273: - `application_roles`
274: - Typed User, Service Account, and Team Assignment tables
275: - Typed User, Service Account, and Team Role Grant tables
276: - OAuth Resource and OAuth Client mapping tables
277: - Service Account OAuth Client credential mappings
278: - `invitations`
279: - `bootstrap_state`
280: - `provisioning_connections`
281: - `provisioning_resource_mappings`
282: - `outbox_events`
283: - `provisioning_deliveries`
284: - `audit_events`
285: 
286: Typed Assignment and Role Grant tables are preferred over nullable polymorphic foreign keys so D1 can enforce referential integrity for each subject type.
287: 
288: Domain records use soft deletion or disabling where identity, ownership, or audit references must remain stable. Relationship records such as membership, Assignment, and Role Grant may be physically deleted after an audit event and outbox event are written.
289: 
290: ## D1 Consistency Strategy
291: 
292: D1 is the source of truth. The implementation must not depend on long-running interactive transactions.
293: 
294: Use:
295: 
296: - Unique constraints for invariants
297: - Foreign keys for relational integrity
298: - Conditional updates for compare-and-swap behavior
299: - `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` for idempotency
300: - `D1Database.batch()` for atomic groups of prepared statements

111: async function consumeM1RateLimit(
112:   database: D1Database,
113:   key: string,
114:   max: number,
115:   windowSeconds: number,
116: ) {
117:   const now = Date.now();
118:   const windowMilliseconds = windowSeconds * 1000;
119:   const bucket = await database
120:     .prepare(
121:       `INSERT INTO rate_limit_buckets
122:         (bucket_key, window_started_at, count, updated_at)
123:        VALUES (?, ?, 1, ?)
124:        ON CONFLICT(bucket_key) DO UPDATE SET
125:          count = CASE
126:            WHEN rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at + ? <= ? THEN 1
127:            ELSE rate_limit_buckets.count + 1
128:          END,
129:          window_started_at = CASE
130:            WHEN rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at + ? <= ? THEN ?
131:            ELSE rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at
132:          END,
133:          updated_at = ?
134:        RETURNING count, window_started_at`,
135:     )
136:     .bind(key, now, now, windowMilliseconds, now, windowMilliseconds, now, now, now)
137:     .first<{ count: number; window_started_at: number }>();
138: 
139:   if (!bucket) throw new M1Error(500);
140: 
141:   if (bucket.count === 1) {
142:     const db = createDb(database);
143:     await db
144:       .delete(rateLimitBuckets)
145:       .where(lt(rateLimitBuckets.updatedAt, now - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000))
146:       .run();
147:   }
148: 
149:   return bucket.count <= max;
150: }

270:     `UPDATE bootstrap_state
271:           SET status = 'user-created', user_id = ?, user_created_at = COALESCE(user_created_at, ?), updated_at = ?
272:         WHERE id = 1

282:     const racedState = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
283:     if (racedState.user_id !== user.id) throw new M1Error(409);

417:   }
418:   if (current.status === "pending" || current.status === "revoked") {

436:   const existingMapping = existingUser

443:   const managedUser = await ensureControlledUser(

447:     body.password,

452:   const marked = await environment.DB.prepare(

454:           SET claimed_user_id = ?, updated_at = ?
455:         WHERE id = ? AND status = 'claimed'
456:           AND (claimed_user_id IS NULL OR claimed_user_id = ?)
457:         RETURNING claimed_user_id`,
458:   )

461:   if (!marked) {

139:               SET status = 'active', disabled_at = NULL, updated_at = ?

12: 
13: export type Actor = {
14:   principalId: string;
15:   userId: string;
16:   roleKeys: Set<string>;
17: };
18: 
19: export async function getActor(auth: AuthInstance, environment: AuthEnvironment, request: Request) {
20:   const session = await auth.api.getSession({
21:     headers: request.headers,
22:     query: { disableCookieCache: true, disableRefresh: true },
23:   });
24:   if (!session?.user || !session.user.emailVerified) throw new M1Error(401);
25: 
26:   const db = createDb(environment.DB);
27:   const principal = await db
28:     .select({ principalId: principals.id, userId: humanPrincipals.userId })
29:     .from(humanPrincipals)
30:     .innerJoin(principals, eq(principals.id, humanPrincipals.principalId))
31:     .where(
32:       and(
33:         eq(humanPrincipals.userId, session.user.id),
34:         eq(humanPrincipals.status, "active"),
35:         eq(humanPrincipals.disabled, false),
36:         eq(principals.type, "human"),
37:         eq(principals.status, "active"),
38:       ),
39:     )
40:     .get();
41:   if (!principal || principal.userId !== session.user.id) throw new M1Error(401);
42: 
43:   const roleRows = await db
44:     .select({ key: systemRoles.key })
45:     .from(systemRoleGrants)
46:     .innerJoin(systemRoles, eq(systemRoles.id, systemRoleGrants.roleId))
47:     .where(
48:       and(
49:         eq(systemRoleGrants.principalId, principal.principalId),
50:         isNull(systemRoleGrants.revokedAt),
51:       ),
52:     )
53:     .all();
54: 
55:   return {
56:     principalId: principal.principalId,
57:     roleKeys: new Set(roleRows.map((row) => row.key)),
58:     userId: session.user.id,
59:   } satisfies Actor;
60: }
61: 
62: export async function requireRole(
63:   auth: AuthInstance,
64:   environment: AuthEnvironment,
65:   request: Request,
66:   roles: readonly string[],
67: ) {
68:   const actor = await getActor(auth, environment, request);
69:   if (!roles.some((role) => actor.roleKeys.has(role))) throw new M1Error(403);
70:   return actor;
71: }

224: async function consumeRateLimit(
225:   database: D1Database,
226:   key: string,
227:   rule: { max: number; window: number },
228: ) {
229:   const now = Date.now();
230:   const windowMilliseconds = rule.window * 1000;
231:   const bucket = await database
232:     .prepare(
233:       `INSERT INTO rate_limit_buckets
234:         (bucket_key, window_started_at, count, updated_at)
235:        VALUES (?, ?, 1, ?)
236:        ON CONFLICT(bucket_key) DO UPDATE SET
237:          count = CASE
238:            WHEN rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at + ? <= ? THEN 1
239:            ELSE rate_limit_buckets.count + 1
240:          END,
241:          window_started_at = CASE
242:            WHEN rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at + ? <= ? THEN ?
243:            ELSE rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at
244:          END,
245:          updated_at = ?
246:        RETURNING count, window_started_at`,
247:     )
248:     .bind(key, now, now, windowMilliseconds, now, windowMilliseconds, now, now, now)
249:     .first<{ count: number; window_started_at: number }>();
250: 
251:   if (!bucket) return { allowed: false, retryAfter: rule.window };
252: 
253:   if (bucket.count === 1) {
254:     const db = createDb(database);
255:     await db
256:       .delete(rateLimitBuckets)
257:       .where(lt(rateLimitBuckets.updatedAt, now - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000))
258:       .run();
259:   }
260: 
261:   const retryAfter = Math.max(
262:     0,
263:     Math.ceil((bucket.window_started_at + windowMilliseconds - now) / 1000),
264:   );
265: 
266:   return {
267:     allowed: bucket.count <= rule.max,
268:     retryAfter,
269:   };
270: }

290: ## D1 Consistency Strategy
291: 
292: D1 is the source of truth. The implementation must not depend on long-running interactive transactions.
293: 
294: Use:
295: 
296: - Unique constraints for invariants
297: - Foreign keys for relational integrity
298: - Conditional updates for compare-and-swap behavior
299: - `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` for idempotency
300: - `D1Database.batch()` for atomic groups of prepared statements
301: - State machines when Better Auth writes and Shui domain writes cannot share one transaction
302: - Reconciliation jobs for cross-system convergence
303: 
304: Every administrative domain mutation writes its audit event and outbox event in the same D1 atomic batch.
305: 
306: Sending to Cloudflare Queues is not atomic with D1. An outbox dispatcher sends pending events to the Queue, and all consumers are idempotent. Duplicate and out-of-order delivery are expected.
307: 
308: ## Bootstrap And Invitations
309: 
310: ### Bootstrap
311: 
312: The first-run setup page is available only while `bootstrap_state` is incomplete. Production setup additionally requires a high-entropy `BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` stored as a Worker secret. The token is submitted in a POST body and never placed in a URL or log.
313: 
314: Bootstrap is an idempotent state machine:
315: 
316: ```text
317: uninitialized -> reserved -> user-created -> completed
318: ```
319: 
320: A singleton unique constraint and conditional writes ensure only one setup request can reserve initialization. Concurrent attempts lose safely. A failed reservation can be resumed only with the bootstrap secret; it is never automatically released to an anonymous caller.
321: 
322: Completion creates the Better Auth User, Human Principal, `root` grant, audit event, and required repair markers. After completion, setup endpoints return not found or redirect to sign-in.
323: 
324: ### Invitations
325: 
326: Public Better Auth sign-up is disabled. A custom invitation flow is the only post-bootstrap User creation path.
327: 
328: Invitation requirements:
329: 
330: - Cryptographically random token
331: - Only a token hash stored in D1
332: - Fixed normalized email address
333: - Explicit expiration
334: - Single-use atomic consumption
335: - Optional initial Team memberships and System Roles
336: - Revocation support
337: - Generic error responses that avoid account enumeration
338: - Idempotent recovery if Better Auth User creation succeeds before domain completion
339: 
340: ## Outbound Provisioning
341: 
342: Provisioning converges each Application toward Shui's desired state. Events are notifications to reconcile current state, not commands that must be applied blindly in event order.
343: 
344: ### Initial SCIM Coverage
345: 
346: - Create and update assigned Users
347: - Set `active: false` when a User loses effective Assignment or is disabled
348: - Create and update Teams as SCIM Groups where supported
349: - Synchronize Team membership
350: - Synchronize Application Role changes through per-Application mapping
351: - Synchronize Assignment changes
352: 
353: SCIM has no universal Application Role attribute. Each provisioning connection therefore defines one of these mappings:
354: 
355: - SCIM Group mapping
356: - Enterprise User extension mapping
357: - Application-specific schema extension
358: - No Role provisioning, leaving Roles available only through OIDC claims
359: 
360: Service Account provisioning is not part of the baseline SCIM User/Group implementation. It requires an explicit Application-specific mapping and is added only for Applications that support non-human SCIM identities.
361: 
362: ### Delivery Behavior
363: 
364: - Queue delivery is treated as at least once
365: - Desired-state version suppresses stale work
366: - Successful external resource IDs are persisted
367: - `429` and transient `5xx` responses retry with bounded exponential backoff
368: - Permanent `4xx` responses become operator-visible failures
369: - Exhausted retries go to a dead-letter queue
370: - Scheduled full reconciliation repairs missed or manually changed state
371: - Provisioning can be paused per Application
372: - Operators can retry or resynchronize an Application
373: 
374: Provisioning credentials are encrypted with AES-GCM using a versioned key stored outside D1 as a Worker secret or Secrets Store secret. Outbound requests require HTTPS, reject redirects, restrict destinations, cap response bodies, and redact credentials and personal data from logs.
375: 
376: ## UI Direction
377: 
378: The UI is a focused identity control plane rather than a generic admin template.
379: 
380: TanStack Start owns routing, SSR, and route-level loading. TanStack Query owns cached server state and mutations, while TanStack Form owns form state. Eden Treaty calls Elysia directly during SSR and over HTTP in the browser. Kumo UI provides accessible, source-tested primitives and semantic tokens, while Shui keeps its own page composition and brand treatment rather than using a generic dashboard template.
381: 
382: Required routes:
383: 
384: - `/setup`
385: - `/sign-in`
386: - `/forgot-password`
387: - `/reset-password`
388: - `/invite/:token`
389: - `/consent`
390: - `/`
391: - `/users`
392: - `/service-accounts`
393: - `/teams`
394: - `/applications`
395: - `/system-roles`
396: - `/audit`
397: 
398: Required quality:
399: 
400: - Distinctive and consistent visual language
401: - Clear Application context during OIDC login and consent
402: - Responsive desktop and mobile layouts
403: - Keyboard navigation and visible focus states
404: - Accessible labels, errors, contrast, and reduced-motion behavior
405: - Complete loading, empty, error, disabled, and destructive-action states
406: - Secret values shown exactly once with explicit acknowledgement
407: - Direct and Team-derived Assignments and Roles visually distinguishable
408: 
409: ## Milestones
410: 
411: ### M0: Compatibility Spike
412: 
413: Purpose: prove the riskiest framework and protocol combination before building domain features.
414: 
415: - [x] Initialize pnpm, TypeScript strict mode, TanStack Start, React 19, Elysia, Wrangler, Drizzle, and Vitest
416: - [x] Pin `better-auth` and every `@better-auth/*` package to `1.7.0-rc.5` without caret ranges
417: - [x] Configure current Workers compatibility date and `nodejs_compat`
418: - [x] Configure `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` for the TanStack Start SSR environment
419: - [x] Mount Elysia in a TanStack Start `/api/$` server route and dispatch every supported HTTP method through `app.fetch(request)`
420: - [x] Configure Eden Treaty for direct SSR calls and browser HTTP calls while preserving request-scoped cookies and headers without cross-request leakage
421: - [x] Configure a custom Worker entrypoint that delegates `fetch` to TanStack Start and exposes `queue` and `scheduled` handlers
422: - [x] Initialize Tailwind CSS v4, Kumo UI, TanStack Form, TanStack Query, and Vite+
423: - [x] Generate binding types with `wrangler types`
424: - [x] Configure local and remote D1 migrations
425: - [x] Mount the Better Auth handler without breaking issuer-path or root `/.well-known` routes
426: - [x] Verify `/api/auth/ok`
427: - [x] Verify OpenID discovery and OAuth Authorization Server metadata
428: - [x] Verify JWKS generation and JWT signature validation
429: - [x] Verify Authorization Code + PKCE against a test client
430: - [x] Verify Client Credentials against a test Resource
431: - [x] Verify Application-specific async custom claims from D1
432: - [x] Verify authorization code single-use behavior under concurrent redemption
433: - [x] Run integration tests inside the Workers runtime
434: - [x] Verify the deployed Staging Worker with remote D1, human sign-in, PKCE, Client Credentials, JWT claims, and concurrent redemption
435: 
436: Exit criteria:
437: 
438: - [x] A real Worker runtime can complete human and M2M token flows
439: - [x] Access Token `aud`, ID Token `aud`, issuer, subject, and claims match the contract
440: - [x] D1 migrations and Better Auth generated schema work locally and remotely
441: - SSR, browser navigation, API requests, Queue handlers, and scheduled handlers coexist in one Worker
442: - No Node-only or TanStack Start/Elysia integration incompatibility remains unexplained
443: 
444: ### M1: Authentication, Setup, And Invitation
445: 
446: - [x] Implement the first-run bootstrap state machine
447: - [x] Require and timing-safely validate `BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN`
448: - [x] Create the first Human Principal and `root` grant
449: - [x] Disable all unrestricted sign-up paths
450: - [x] Implement invitation creation, revocation, expiration, and atomic consumption
451: - [x] Implement password reset and email verification
452: - [x] Implement User disablement and session revocation
453: - [x] Add authentication and bootstrap audit events
454: - [x] Build setup, sign-in, invitation, and password recovery screens
455: - [x] Add rate limits for setup, sign-in, invitations, and password reset
456: 
457: Exit criteria:
458: 
459: - Concurrent setup attempts produce exactly one initial `root`
460: - Direct calls to public sign-up fail after and before bootstrap unless they use the controlled setup/invitation flow
461: - An invitation cannot be reused, accepted by another email, or accepted after expiration
462: - Interrupted setup and invitation flows can safely resume or reconcile
463: - The last active `root` invariant is enforced
464: 
465: ### M2: Principals, Teams, And System Roles
466: 
467: - [ ] Implement Principal lifecycle and Human Principal repair
468: - [ ] Implement Service Account lifecycle and User/Team ownership
469: - [ ] Implement flat Teams and User membership
470: - [ ] Seed built-in System Roles
471: - [ ] Implement System Role authorization guards in Elysia
472: - [ ] Implement ownership transfer before owner deletion or disablement
473: - [ ] Add audit events for all mutations
474: - [ ] Build Users, Service Accounts, Teams, and System Roles administration
475: 
476: Exit criteria:
477: 
478: - Service Accounts cannot authenticate as human Users
479: - Service Accounts cannot become Team members
480: - Teams cannot contain Teams
481: - User and Team owners are enforced by foreign keys and application validation
482: - Every protected management operation maps to a documented System Role permission
483: 
484: ### M3: Applications, Assignments, And Roles
485: 
486: - [ ] Implement Application lifecycle and ownership
487: - [ ] Implement one OAuth Resource per Application
488: - [ ] Implement Human OIDC Client management
489: - [ ] Implement dynamic Application Roles
490: - [ ] Implement typed User, Service Account, and Team Assignments
491: - [ ] Implement typed direct and Team Role Grants
492: - [ ] Implement effective Assignment queries
493: - [ ] Implement effective Role queries with all origins
494: - [ ] Increment `authz_version` on authorization-affecting changes
495: - [ ] Build Application, Assignment, Role, and origin-aware administration UI
496: 
497: Exit criteria:
498: 
499: - Assigned without Roles is distinct from not assigned
500: - Team Assignment grants effective access to active Team members
501: - Direct and Team Role origins are returned separately
502: - Duplicate Role origins collapse into one claim value without losing administration provenance
503: - Team removal and membership removal update effective access immediately for new token issuance
504: 
505: ### M4: Application OIDC And Service Accounts
506: 
507: - [ ] Link every managed Client to exactly one allowed Application Resource
508: - [ ] Reject token issuance when Assignment is absent or suspended
509: - [ ] Emit only target-Application Roles and Teams
510: - [ ] Implement namespaced Principal and authorization claims
511: - [ ] Implement Service Account OAuth Client credential creation
512: - [ ] Display Client secrets once and never log them
513: - [ ] Implement overlapping credential rotation and disablement
514: - [ ] Deny credentials for disabled Service Accounts or Applications
515: - [ ] Publish a downstream token-verification integration guide
516: - [ ] Add a reference relying-party test Application
517: 
518: Exit criteria:
519: 
520: - Application A never receives Application B's Roles, Teams, or identifiers
521: - Human Access Tokens and M2M Access Tokens validate with the same JWKS
522: - M2M `sub` changes with a rotated credential while namespaced `principal_id` remains stable
523: - Resource, issuer, audience, expiration, and scope validation failures are covered by tests
524: - Disabled credentials cannot issue new tokens

526: ### M5: Outbound SCIM Provisioning
527: 
528: - [ ] Implement encrypted provisioning connection storage
529: - [ ] Implement desired-state projections for Users, Teams, memberships, Assignments, and Roles
530: - [ ] Write mutation, audit, and outbox records in one D1 batch
531: - [ ] Implement an outbox dispatcher to Cloudflare Queues
532: - [ ] Implement an idempotent provisioning Queue consumer
533: - [ ] Implement SCIM User create, update, and deactivate
534: - [ ] Implement SCIM Group and membership synchronization
535: - [ ] Implement configurable Role mapping
536: - [ ] Persist external resource IDs and desired-state versions

538: - [ ] Implement scheduled full reconciliation
539: - [ ] Build provisioning status, failure, pause, retry, and resync UI

541: Exit criteria:
542: 
543: - Duplicate and reversed messages converge to the latest desired state
544: - `429`, timeout, `5xx`, conflict, missing resource, and permanent `4xx` behavior is tested
545: - Assignment removal deactivates the downstream User without deleting Shui identity data
546: - Team membership and Role changes converge after transient failures
547: - No provisioning credential or sensitive response body appears in logs

549: ### M6: Security And Operations Hardening
550: 
551: - [ ] Enable structured Workers logs and traces
552: - [ ] Add correlation IDs across API, audit, outbox, Queue, and SCIM delivery
553: - [ ] Configure database-backed rate limiting suitable for Workers
554: - [ ] Review CSRF, origin, cookie, and canonical issuer configuration
555: - [ ] Add short JWT lifetimes and document delayed revocation semantics
556: - [ ] Configure JWKS rotation and grace period
557: - [ ] Add backup, D1 Time Travel, restore, and migration procedures
558: - [ ] Add secret rotation procedures for Better Auth, bootstrap, encryption, OAuth Clients, and SCIM
559: - [ ] Add retention policies for audit, delivery, invitation, and expired token data
560: - [ ] Add health and readiness checks that do not expose secrets
561: - [ ] Complete threat modeling and dependency review

563: Exit criteria:
564: 
565: - Recovery procedures have been executed in staging
566: - Key rotation preserves verification during the grace period
567: - Security-sensitive endpoints have explicit abuse tests
568: - Audit records cover every privileged mutation and credential lifecycle event
569: - Operational dashboards expose authentication failures, Queue backlog, provisioning failures, and D1 errors
570: 
571: ### M7: Release Candidate And Launch
572: 
573: - [ ] Run the OpenID conformance tests applicable to supported flows
574: - [ ] Run SCIM integration tests against representative mock and real Applications
575: - [ ] Run accessibility, mobile, and cross-browser UI tests

590: ## Testing Strategy
591: 
592: ### Unit Tests
593: 
594: - Effective Assignment matrix

605: Use `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` with real D1 and Queue bindings where possible.
606: 
607: - Better Auth session and endpoint behavior

609: - OIDC discovery, authorization, token, UserInfo, and JWKS
610: - Concurrent bootstrap and authorization code consumption

613: 
614: ### End-To-End Tests
615: 
616: - First-run setup
617: - Sign-in and password reset
618: - Invitation acceptance
619: - Team-derived Assignment and Role changes
620: - OIDC login from a reference Application
621: - Service Account credential creation and rotation
622: - Provisioning failure and operator retry
623: - Responsive and keyboard-only administration flows
624: 
625: ### Security Tests
626: 
627: - Account and invitation enumeration
628: - CSRF and untrusted Origin rejection
629: - Redirect URI exact matching
630: - PKCE, state, and nonce validation
631: - Wrong issuer and audience rejection
632: - Cross-Application Role leakage
633: - Setup and invitation races
634: - Secret redaction
635: - SCIM SSRF and redirect rejection
636: - JWT behavior after Principal, Assignment, Role, Client, or Application disablement
637: 
638: ## Known Risks
639: 
640: | Risk | Mitigation |
641: | --- | --- |
642: | Better Auth 1.7 is an RC | Exact version pinning, schema snapshots, compatibility spike, reviewed upgrades only |
643: | Elysia's direct Workers adapter is experimental | Embed Elysia through the documented TanStack Start route integration, keep a standard Fetch boundary, and run workerd integration tests |
644: | TanStack Start and Elysia add two server abstractions | Keep all domain APIs and business logic in Elysia, use Start only for web delivery and SSR orchestration, and test route ownership explicitly |
645: | Better Auth and domain writes cannot always share one transaction | Idempotent state machines, fail-closed authorization, reconciliation |
646: | D1 has limited transaction patterns and per-database serial throughput | Atomic batches, indexed short queries, no long transactions, production-like load tests |
647: | Queue delivery is at least once | Transactional outbox, idempotency keys, desired-state reconciliation |
648: | JWT Role changes are not instant | Short lifetimes, `authz_version`, optional live validation for high-risk Applications |
649: | OAuth Client secret rotation invalidates the old secret immediately | Overlapping multiple Client credentials per Service Account |
650: | SCIM Role representation differs by Application | Explicit versioned mapping per provisioning connection |
651: | First public deployment can be claimed before the owner arrives | Required Worker-secret bootstrap token and atomic singleton reservation |

1: # @elysiajs/eden
2: Fully type-safe Elysia client refers to the [documentation](https://elysiajs.com/eden/overview)
3: 
4: ## Installation
5: ```bash
6: bun add elysia @elysiajs/eden

      FROM invitations
     WHERE id = ? AND status = 'expired' AND claimed_user_id IS NOT NULL
       AND expired_at = ?`;

    database
      .prepare(
        `UPDATE invitations
          SET status = 'expired', expired_at = ?, updated_at = ?
        WHERE id = ?
          AND expired_at IS NULL
          AND ((status IN ('pending', 'claimed') AND expires_at <= ?) OR status = 'expired')`,
      )
      .bind(now, now, invitation.id, now),
    database
      .prepare(
        `UPDATE human_principals
          SET status = 'disabled', disabled = 1, disabled_at = ?, updated_at = ?
        WHERE principal_id = (${principalSubquery})`,
      )
      .bind(now, now, invitation.id, now),
    database
      .prepare(
        `UPDATE principals
          SET status = 'disabled', disabled_at = ?, updated_at = ?
        WHERE id = (${principalSubquery}) AND status = 'active'`,
      )
      .bind(now, now, invitation.id, now),
    database
      .prepare(
        `DELETE FROM session
        WHERE user_id = (

             AND expired_at = ?
          )`,

      .bind(invitation.id, now),

      .prepare(
        `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO audit_events
         (id, event_type, actor_principal_id, subject_principal_id, subject_user_id, metadata, created_at)
         SELECT ?, 'invitation.expired', NULL,
                (SELECT id FROM principals WHERE id = COALESCE(i.claimed_principal_id, 'human_' || i.claimed_user_id)),

           FROM invitations AS i
          WHERE i.id = ? AND i.status = 'expired' AND i.expired_at = ?`,
      )
      .bind(
        `invitation:expired:${invitation.id}`,
        JSON.stringify({ invitationId: invitation.id }),
        now,
        invitation.id,
        now,
      ),
    database
      .prepare(
        `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO outbox_events
         (id, dedupe_key, event_type, aggregate_type, aggregate_id, payload, status, attempts, available_at, created_at)
         SELECT ?, ?, 'invitation.expired', 'invitation', ?, ?, 'pending', 0, ?, ?

  ]);

export async function expireStaleInvitations(database: D1Database) {
  const now = Date.now();
  const invitationsToExpire = await database
    .prepare(
      `SELECT id
         FROM invitations
        WHERE (status IN ('pending', 'claimed') AND expires_at <= ?)
           OR (status = 'expired' AND expired_at IS NULL)`,
    )
    .bind(now)
    .all<{ id: string }>();

  for (const invitation of invitationsToExpire.results) {
    await expireInvitation(database, invitation, now);
  }
}

async function createInvitation(
  environment: AuthEnvironment,
  actor: Actor,
  body: InvitationCreateBody,
  request: Request,
) {
  await enforceRateLimit(environment, request, "invitation-create", 30, 60);
  const email = normalizeEmail(body.email);
  const name = body.name ? normalizeName(body.name, email) : null;
  const requestedRoleKeys = await validateRoleKeys(environment.DB, body.systemRoleKeys ?? []);
  const now = Date.now();
  const staleInvitations = await createDb(environment.DB)
    .select({ expiresAt: invitations.expiresAt, id: invitations.id })
    .from(invitations)
    .where(
      and(
        eq(invitations.email, email),
        inArray(invitations.status, ["pending", "claimed"]),
        lte(invitations.expiresAt, now),
      ),
    )
    .all();
  for (const staleInvitation of staleInvitations) {
    await expireInvitation(environment.DB, staleInvitation, now);
  }
  const existingMapping = await createDb(environment.DB)
    .select({ userId: humanPrincipals.userId })
    .from(humanPrincipals)
    .innerJoin(principals, eq(principals.id, humanPrincipals.principalId))
    .innerJoin(user, eq(user.id, humanPrincipals.userId))
    .where(
      and(
        eq(user.email, email),
        eq(principals.status, "active"),
        eq(humanPrincipals.status, "active"),
        eq(humanPrincipals.disabled, false),
      ),
    )
    .get();
  if (existingMapping) throw new M1Error(409);
  const existingInvitation = await createDb(environment.DB)
    .select({ id: invitations.id })
    .from(invitations)
    .where(and(eq(invitations.email, email), inArray(invitations.status, ["pending", "claimed"])))
    .get();
  if (existingInvitation) throw new M1Error(409);

  const token = randomToken();
  const tokenHash = await sha256Base64Url(token);
  const invitationId = crypto.randomUUID();
  const requestedLifetime = body.expiresInSeconds ?? body.expiresIn ?? 60 * 60 * 24 * 7;
  const expiresAt = now + requestedLifetime * 1000;

  try {
    await environment.DB.batch([
      environment.DB.prepare(
        `INSERT INTO invitations
            (id, token_hash, email, name, status, expires_at, invited_by_principal_id, system_role_keys, created_at, updated_at)
           VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'pending', ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)`,
      ).bind(
        invitationId,
        tokenHash,
        email,
        name,
        expiresAt,
        actor.principalId,
        JSON.stringify(requestedRoleKeys),
        now,
        now,
      ),
      auditStatement(
        environment.DB,
        `invitation:created:${invitationId}`,
        "invitation.created",
        actor.principalId,
        null,
        null,
        { email, expiresAt },
        now,
      ),
      outboxStatement(
        environment.DB,
        `invitation:created:outbox:${invitationId}`,
        "invitation.created",
        "invitation",
        invitationId,
        { email, expiresAt },
        now,
      ),
    ]);
  } catch (error) {
    const conflictingInvitation = await createDb(environment.DB)
      .select({ id: invitations.id })
      .from(invitations)
      .where(and(eq(invitations.email, email), inArray(invitations.status, ["pending", "claimed"])))
      .get();
    if (conflictingInvitation) throw new M1Error(409);
    throw error;
  }

  let deliveryPending = false;
  try {
    await sendInvitationEmail(environment, { email, expiresAt, name, token });
  } catch (error) {
    deliveryPending = true;
    await environment.DB.prepare(
      `UPDATE outbox_events
            SET status = 'failed', attempts = attempts + 1, last_error = ?, available_at = ?
          WHERE dedupe_key = ?`,
    )
      .bind(
        error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Invitation delivery failed.",
        Date.now(),
        `invitation:created:outbox:${invitationId}`,
      )
      .run();
  }
  return { deliveryPending, email, expiresAt, id: invitationId, token };
}

async function getPublicInvitation(environment: AuthEnvironment, token: string, request: Request) {
  await enforceRateLimit(environment, request, "invitation-read", 60, 60);
  const invitation = await readInvitation(environment.DB, await sha256Base64Url(token));
  if (!invitation) throw new M1Error(404);
  const now = Date.now();
  if (
    (invitation.status === "pending" || invitation.status === "claimed") &&
    invitation.expires_at <= now
  ) {
    await expireInvitation(environment.DB, invitation, now);
    throw new M1Error(404);
  }
  if (invitation.status === "expired") {
    await expireInvitation(environment.DB, invitation, now);
    throw new M1Error(404);
  }
  if (invitation.status !== "pending" && invitation.status !== "claimed") throw new M1Error(404);
  return {
    email: invitation.email,
    expiresAt: invitation.expires_at,
    name: invitation.name,
    status: invitation.status,
  };
}

                  system_role_keys, claimed_at`,

  if (current.status === "completed") throw new M1Error(409);

  const existingUser = await createDb(environment.DB)
    .select({ id: user.id })
    .from(user)
    .where(eq(user.email, current.email))
    .get();
  const existingMapping = existingUser
    ? await readHumanMapping(environment.DB, existingUser.id)
    : undefined;
  const hasActiveMapping =
    existingMapping?.principal_status === "active" &&
    existingMapping.human_status === "active" &&
    existingMapping.disabled === 0;
  const managedUser = await ensureControlledUser(
    auth,
    current.email,
    normalizeName(body.name, current.name ?? current.email),
    body.password,
    current.claimed_user_id,
    Boolean(current.claimed_user_id) || !hasActiveMapping,
    current.claimed_at,
  );
  const marked = await environment.DB.prepare(
    `UPDATE invitations
          SET claimed_user_id = ?, updated_at = ?
        WHERE id = ? AND status = 'claimed'
          AND (claimed_user_id IS NULL OR claimed_user_id = ?)
        RETURNING claimed_user_id`,
  )
    .bind(managedUser.id, Date.now(), current.id, managedUser.id)
    .first<{ claimed_user_id: string }>();
  if (!marked) {
    const racedInvitation = await readInvitation(environment.DB, current.token_hash);
    if (!racedInvitation || racedInvitation.claimed_user_id !== managedUser.id)
      throw new M1Error(409);
    current = racedInvitation;
  } else {
    current = (await readInvitation(environment.DB, current.token_hash)) ?? current;
  }
  if (current.status !== "claimed") throw new M1Error(409);

  const roleKeys = await validateRoleKeys(
    environment.DB,
    roleKeysFromStorage(current.system_role_keys),
  );
  await sendVerificationEmail(auth, managedUser);
  const principalId = await ensureHumanPrincipal(
    environment.DB,
    managedUser.id,
    Date.now(),
    true,
    current.id,
  );
  const eventId = `invitation:completed:${current.id}`;
  const completedAt = Date.now();
  const statements = [
    environment.DB.prepare(
      `UPDATE invitations
          SET status = 'completed', claimed_principal_id = ?, completed_at = ?, updated_at = ?
          WHERE id = ? AND status = 'claimed' AND claimed_user_id = ?
            AND expires_at > ?
        RETURNING id`,
    ).bind(principalId, completedAt, completedAt, current.id, managedUser.id, completedAt),
    ...roleKeys.map((roleKey) =>
      grantInvitationRoleStatement(
        environment.DB,
        current.id,
        managedUser.id,
        principalId,
        roleKey,
        current.invited_by_principal_id,
        completedAt,
      ),
    ),
    auditStatementWhen(
      environment.DB,
      eventId,
      "invitation.completed",
      current.invited_by_principal_id,
      principalId,
      managedUser.id,
      { email: current.email },
      completedAt,
      "SELECT 1 FROM invitations WHERE id = ? AND status = 'completed' AND claimed_user_id = ?",
      [current.id, managedUser.id],
    ),
    outboxStatementWhen(
      environment.DB,
      `invitation:completed:outbox:${current.id}`,
      "invitation.completed",
      "invitation",
      current.id,
      { principalId, userId: managedUser.id },
      completedAt,
      "SELECT 1 FROM invitations WHERE id = ? AND status = 'completed' AND claimed_user_id = ?",
      [current.id, managedUser.id],
    ),
  ];
  const results = await environment.DB.batch(statements);
  const completionResult = results[0];
  if (!completionResult?.results.length) {
    await expireInvitation(environment.DB, current, completedAt);
    throw new M1Error(409);
  }
  return {
    email: managedUser.email,
    principalId,
    status: "accepted" as const,
    userId: managedUser.id,
  };
}

async function resolveInvitationForRevoke(database: D1Database, identifier: string) {
  const db = createDb(database);
  const byId = await db
    .select({ id: invitations.id, status: invitations.status })
    .from(invitations)
    .where(eq(invitations.id, identifier))
    .get();
  if (byId) return byId;
  const tokenHash = await sha256Base64Url(identifier);
  return db
    .select({ id: invitations.id, status: invitations.status })
    .from(invitations)
    .where(eq(invitations.tokenHash, tokenHash))
    .get();
}

async function revokeInvitation(
  environment: AuthEnvironment,
  actor: Actor,
  identifier: string,
  request: Request,
) {
  await enforceRateLimit(environment, request, "invitation-revoke", 30, 60);
  const invitation = await resolveInvitationForRevoke(environment.DB, identifier);
  if (!invitation) throw new M1Error(404);
  const now = Date.now();
  const principalSubquery = `
    SELECT COALESCE(claimed_principal_id, 'human_' || claimed_user_id)
      FROM invitations
     WHERE id = ? AND status = 'revoked' AND revoked_at = ? AND claimed_user_id IS NOT NULL`;
  const results = await environment.DB.batch([
    environment.DB.prepare(
      `UPDATE invitations
            SET status = 'revoked', revoked_at = ?, updated_at = ?
           WHERE id = ?
             AND revoked_at IS NULL
             AND status IN ('pending', 'claimed', 'revoked')
           RETURNING id`,
    ).bind(now, now, invitation.id),
    environment.DB.prepare(
      `UPDATE human_principals
          SET status = 'disabled', disabled = 1, disabled_at = ?, updated_at = ?
        WHERE principal_id = (${principalSubquery})`,
    ).bind(now, now, invitation.id, now),
    environment.DB.prepare(
      `UPDATE principals
          SET status = 'disabled', disabled_at = ?, updated_at = ?
        WHERE id = (${principalSubquery}) AND status = 'active'`,
    ).bind(now, now, invitation.id, now),
    environment.DB.prepare(
      `DELETE FROM session
        WHERE user_id = (
          SELECT claimed_user_id
            FROM invitations
           WHERE id = ? AND status = 'revoked' AND revoked_at = ? AND claimed_user_id IS NOT NULL
        )`,
    ).bind(invitation.id, now),
    auditStatementWhen(
      environment.DB,
      `invitation:revoked:${invitation.id}`,
      "invitation.revoked",
      actor.principalId,
      null,
      null,
      { invitationId: invitation.id },
      now,
      "SELECT 1 FROM invitations WHERE id = ? AND status = 'revoked' AND revoked_at = ?",
      [invitation.id, now],
    ),
    outboxStatementWhen(
      environment.DB,
      `invitation:revoked:outbox:${invitation.id}`,
      "invitation.revoked",
      "invitation",
      invitation.id,
      {},
      now,
      "SELECT 1 FROM invitations WHERE id = ? AND status = 'revoked' AND revoked_at = ?",
      [invitation.id, now],
    ),
  ]);
  if (!results[0]?.results.length) {
    const current = await resolveInvitationForRevoke(environment.DB, identifier);
    if (current?.status !== "revoked") throw new M1Error(409);
  }
  return { id: invitation.id, status: "revoked" as const };
}

180: function assertMutationOrigin(environment: AuthEnvironment, request: Request) {
181:   if (request.headers.get("sec-fetch-site") === "cross-site") throw new M1Error(403);

186: 
187:   const referer = request.headers.get("referer");
188:   if (!origin && referer) {
189:     try {
190:       if (new URL(referer).origin !== expectedOrigin) throw new M1Error(403);
191:     } catch (error) {
192:       if (error instanceof M1Error) throw error;
193:       throw new M1Error(403);
194:     }
195:   }

172:     environment.DB.prepare(
173:       `UPDATE bootstrap_state
174:               SET status = 'reserved', reservation_id = ?, reserved_at = ?, updated_at = ?
175:             WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'uninitialized'
176:             RETURNING reservation_id, status`,
177:     ).bind(reservationId, now, now),

179:       environment.DB,

181:       "bootstrap.reserved",
182:       null,
183:       null,
184:       null,
185:       {},

188:       [reservationId, now],

190:     outboxStatementWhen(
191:       environment.DB,
192:       `bootstrap:reserved:outbox:${reservationId}`,
193:       "bootstrap.reserved",
194:       "bootstrap",
195:       "1",
196:       { reservationId },
197:       now,
198:       "SELECT 1 FROM bootstrap_state WHERE id = 1 AND status = 'reserved' AND reservation_id = ? AND reserved_at = ?",
199:       [reservationId, now],
200:     ),
201:   ]);
202:   const reserved = results[0]?.results[0] as
203:     | { reservation_id: string; status: BootstrapStatus }
204:     | undefined;
205: 
206:   if (!reserved) {
207:     const racedState = await getBootstrapState(environment.DB);
208:     if (racedState.status === "completed" || !racedState.reservation_id) throw new M1Error(409);
209:     return { reservationId: racedState.reservation_id, status: racedState.status };
210:   }

212:   return { reservationId, status: reserved.status };

238:   ) {
239:     throw new M1Error(400);
240:   }

379: export async function claimInvitationWithAuth(
380:   environment: AuthEnvironment,
381:   auth: AuthInstance,
382:   token: string,
383:   body: InvitationAcceptBody,
384:   request: Request,
385: ) {
386:   await enforceRateLimit(environment, request, "invitation-accept", 30, 60);
387:   const invitation = await readInvitation(environment.DB, await sha256Base64Url(token));
388:   if (!invitation) throw new M1Error(404);
389:   const now = Date.now();
390:   const suppliedEmail = body.email ? normalizeEmail(body.email) : invitation.email;
391:   if (suppliedEmail !== invitation.email) throw new M1Error(400);
392:   const context = await auth.$context;
393:   if (
394:     body.password.length < context.password.config.minPasswordLength ||
395:     body.password.length > context.password.config.maxPasswordLength
396:   ) {
397:     throw new M1Error(400);
398:   }
399: 
400:   let current = invitation;
401:   if (current.status === "pending") {
402:     if (current.expires_at <= now) {
403:       await expireInvitation(environment.DB, current, now);
404:       throw new M1Error(404);
405:     }
406:     const claimed = await environment.DB.prepare(
407:       `UPDATE invitations
408:             SET status = 'claimed', claimed_at = ?, updated_at = ?
409:           WHERE id = ? AND status = 'pending' AND expires_at > ?
410:         RETURNING id, token_hash, email, name, status, expires_at,
411:                   invited_by_principal_id, claimed_user_id, claimed_principal_id,
412:                   system_role_keys, claimed_at`,
413:     )
414:       .bind(now, now, current.id, now)
415:       .first<Invitation>();
416:     current = claimed ?? (await readInvitation(environment.DB, current.token_hash)) ?? current;
417:   }
418:   if (current.status === "pending" || current.status === "revoked") {
419:     throw new M1Error(409);
420:   }
421:   if (current.status === "expired") {
422:     await expireInvitation(environment.DB, current, now);
423:     throw new M1Error(409);
424:   }
425:   if (current.expires_at <= now) {
426:     await expireInvitation(environment.DB, current, now);
427:     throw new M1Error(409);
428:   }
429:   if (current.status === "completed") throw new M1Error(409);
430: 
431:   const existingUser = await createDb(environment.DB)
432:     .select({ id: user.id })
433:     .from(user)
434:     .where(eq(user.email, current.email))
435:     .get();
436:   const existingMapping = existingUser
437:     ? await readHumanMapping(environment.DB, existingUser.id)
438:     : undefined;
439:   const hasActiveMapping =
440:     existingMapping?.principal_status === "active" &&
441:     existingMapping.human_status === "active" &&
442:     existingMapping.disabled === 0;
443:   const managedUser = await ensureControlledUser(
444:     auth,
445:     current.email,
446:     normalizeName(body.name, current.name ?? current.email),
447:     body.password,
448:     current.claimed_user_id,
449:     Boolean(current.claimed_user_id) || !hasActiveMapping,
450:     current.claimed_at,
451:   );
452:   const marked = await environment.DB.prepare(
453:     `UPDATE invitations
454:           SET claimed_user_id = ?, updated_at = ?
455:         WHERE id = ? AND status = 'claimed'
456:           AND (claimed_user_id IS NULL OR claimed_user_id = ?)
457:         RETURNING claimed_user_id`,
458:   )
459:     .bind(managedUser.id, Date.now(), current.id, managedUser.id)
460:     .first<{ claimed_user_id: string }>();
461:   if (!marked) {
462:     const racedInvitation = await readInvitation(environment.DB, current.token_hash);
463:     if (!racedInvitation || racedInvitation.claimed_user_id !== managedUser.id)
464:       throw new M1Error(409);
465:     current = racedInvitation;
466:   } else {
467:     current = (await readInvitation(environment.DB, current.token_hash)) ?? current;
468:   }
469:   if (current.status !== "claimed") throw new M1Error(409);
470: 
471:   const roleKeys = await validateRoleKeys(
472:     environment.DB,
473:     roleKeysFromStorage(current.system_role_keys),
474:   );
475:   await sendVerificationEmail(auth, managedUser);
476:   const principalId = await ensureHumanPrincipal(
477:     environment.DB,
478:     managedUser.id,
479:     Date.now(),
480:     true,
481:     current.id,
482:     (database, invitationId, expirationNow) =>
483:       expireInvitation(database, { id: invitationId }, expirationNow),
484:   );
485:   const eventId = `invitation:completed:${current.id}`;
486:   const completedAt = Date.now();
487:   const statements = [
488:     environment.DB.prepare(
489:       `UPDATE invitations
490:           SET status = 'completed', claimed_principal_id = ?, completed_at = ?, updated_at = ?
491:           WHERE id = ? AND status = 'claimed' AND claimed_user_id = ?
492:             AND expires_at > ?
493:         RETURNING id`,
494:     ).bind(principalId, completedAt, completedAt, current.id, managedUser.id, completedAt),
495:     ...roleKeys.map((roleKey) =>
496:       grantInvitationRoleStatement(
497:         environment.DB,
498:         current.id,
499:         managedUser.id,
500:         principalId,
501:         roleKey,
502:         current.invited_by_principal_id,
503:         completedAt,
504:       ),
505:     ),
506:     auditStatementWhen(
507:       environment.DB,
508:       eventId,
509:       "invitation.completed",
510:       current.invited_by_principal_id,
511:       principalId,
512:       managedUser.id,
513:       { email: current.email },
514:       completedAt,
515:       "SELECT 1 FROM invitations WHERE id = ? AND status = 'completed' AND claimed_user_id = ?",
516:       [current.id, managedUser.id],
517:     ),
518:     outboxStatementWhen(
519:       environment.DB,
520:       `invitation:completed:outbox:${current.id}`,
521:       "invitation.completed",
522:       "invitation",
523:       current.id,
524:       { principalId, userId: managedUser.id },
525:       completedAt,
526:       "SELECT 1 FROM invitations WHERE id = ? AND status = 'completed' AND claimed_user_id = ?",
527:       [current.id, managedUser.id],
528:     ),
529:   ];
530:   const results = await environment.DB.batch(statements);
531:   const completionResult = results[0];
532:   if (!completionResult?.results.length) {
533:     await expireInvitation(environment.DB, current, completedAt);
534:     throw new M1Error(409);
535:   }
536:   return {
537:     email: managedUser.email,
538:     principalId,
539:     status: "accepted" as const,
540:     userId: managedUser.id,
541:   };
542: }

138: export async function ensureHumanPrincipal(

171:   }
172:   const needsReactivation =
173:     existingPrincipal?.status === "disabled" ||
174:     Boolean(
175:       existingMapping &&
176:       (existingMapping.human_status !== "active" || existingMapping.disabled !== 0),
177:     );
178:   if (allowDisabled && needsReactivation && existingPrincipal) {

79: export async function setUserDisabled(
80:   environment: AuthEnvironment,
81:   actor: Actor,
82:   identifier: string,
83:   disabled: boolean,
84:   request: Request,
85: ) {
86:   await enforceRateLimit(environment, request, disabled ? "user-disable" : "user-enable", 60, 60);
87:   const target = await resolveHumanPrincipal(environment.DB, identifier);
88:   if (!target) throw new M1Error(404);
89:   if (
90:     target.principal_status === (disabled ? "disabled" : "active") &&
91:     target.human_status === (disabled ? "disabled" : "active")
92:   ) {
93:     if (disabled) {
94:       await environment.DB.prepare("DELETE FROM session WHERE user_id = ?")
95:         .bind(target.user_id)
96:         .run();
97:     }
98:     return {
99:       status: disabled ? ("disabled" as const) : ("active" as const),
100:       userId: target.user_id,
101:     };
102:   }
103:   if (disabled && target.is_root === 1 && (await activeRootCount(environment.DB)) <= 1) {
104:     throw new M1Error(409);
105:   }
106: 
107:   const now = Date.now();
108:   const nextStatus = disabled ? "disabled" : "active";
109:   const mutation = environment.DB.prepare(
110:     disabled
111:       ? `UPDATE principals
112:               SET status = 'disabled', disabled_at = ?, updated_at = ?
113:             WHERE id = ? AND type = 'human' AND status = 'active'
114:               AND (
115:                 NOT EXISTS (
116:                   SELECT 1
117:                     FROM system_role_grants AS own_grant
118:                     JOIN system_roles AS own_role ON own_role.id = own_grant.role_id
119:                    WHERE own_grant.principal_id = principals.id
120:                      AND own_grant.revoked_at IS NULL
121:                      AND own_role.key = 'root'
122:                 )
123:                 OR (
124:                   SELECT COUNT(*)
125:                     FROM principals AS root_principal
126:                     JOIN human_principals AS root_human ON root_human.principal_id = root_principal.id
127:                     JOIN system_role_grants AS root_grant ON root_grant.principal_id = root_principal.id
128:                     JOIN system_roles AS root_role ON root_role.id = root_grant.role_id
129:                    WHERE root_principal.type = 'human'
130:                      AND root_principal.status = 'active'
131:                      AND root_human.status = 'active'
132:                      AND root_human.disabled = 0
133:                      AND root_grant.revoked_at IS NULL
134:                      AND root_role.key = 'root'
135:                 ) > 1
136:               )
137:             RETURNING id`
138:       : `UPDATE principals
139:               SET status = 'active', disabled_at = NULL, updated_at = ?
140:              WHERE id = ? AND type = 'human' AND status = 'disabled'
141:              RETURNING id`,
142:   ).bind(...(disabled ? [now, now, target.principal_id] : [now, target.principal_id]));
143: 
144:   const results = await environment.DB.batch([
145:     mutation,
146:     environment.DB.prepare(
147:       `UPDATE human_principals
148:           SET status = ?, disabled = ?, disabled_at = ?, updated_at = ?
149:           WHERE principal_id = ?
150:             AND EXISTS (
151:               SELECT 1 FROM principals

153:             )`,

155:       nextStatus,
156:       disabled ? 1 : 0,
157:       disabled ? now : null,
158:       now,
159:       target.principal_id,
160:       target.principal_id,
161:       nextStatus,
162:       now,
163:     ),
164:     ...(disabled
165:       ? [environment.DB.prepare("DELETE FROM session WHERE user_id = ?").bind(target.user_id)]
166:       : []),
167:     auditStatementWhen(
168:       environment.DB,
169:       `user:${disabled ? "disabled" : "enabled"}:${target.principal_id}:${now}`,
170:       `user.${disabled ? "disabled" : "enabled"}`,

177:       [target.principal_id, nextStatus, now],
178:     ),

182:       `user.${disabled ? "disabled" : "enabled"}`,

188:       [target.principal_id, nextStatus, now],

1: import { Elysia, t } from "elysia";
2: 
3: import { type AuthEnvironment, createAuth } from "./auth";
4: import { createM1Routes } from "./m1";
5: 
6: export function createApiApp(environment: AuthEnvironment) {
7:   const auth = createAuth(environment);
8: 
9:   return new Elysia({ aot: false, prefix: "/api" })
10:     .onRequest(async ({ request }) => requireApiResource(request))
11:     .use(createM1Routes(environment, auth))
12:     .get("/health", () => ({ service: "shui-api", status: "ok" as const }), {
13:       response: t.Object({
14:         service: t.String(),
15:         status: t.Literal("ok"),
16:       }),
17:     })
18:     .head("/health", () => new Response(null, { status: 204 }))
19:     .mount(auth.handler);
20: }
21: 
22: export type ApiApp = ReturnType<typeof createApiApp>;
23: 
24: async function requireApiResource(request: Request) {
25:   const url = new URL(request.url);
26:   const isAuthorize = url.pathname.endsWith("/oauth2/authorize");
27:   const isToken = url.pathname.endsWith("/oauth2/token");
28:   if (!isAuthorize && !isToken) return;
29: 
30:   if (isAuthorize) {
31:     const params = request.method === "GET" ? url.searchParams : await readOAuthBody(request);
32:     const scopes = params.get("scope")?.split(/\s+/) ?? [];
33:     if (scopes.includes("api:read") && !params.getAll("resource").some(Boolean)) {
34:       return invalidResourceResponse();
35:     }
36:     return;
37:   }
38: 
39:   const body = await readOAuthBody(request);
40:   if (body.get("grant_type") === "client_credentials" && !body.getAll("resource").some(Boolean)) {
41:     return invalidResourceResponse();
42:   }
43: }
44: 
45: async function readOAuthBody(request: Request) {
46:   const contentType = request.headers.get("content-type") ?? "";
47:   if (contentType.includes("application/x-www-form-urlencoded")) {
48:     return new URLSearchParams(await request.clone().text());
49:   }
50: 
51:   if (contentType.includes("application/json")) {
52:     const body = (await request
53:       .clone()
54:       .json()
55:       .catch(() => null)) as Record<string, unknown> | null;
56:     const params = new URLSearchParams();
57:     if (typeof body?.grant_type === "string") params.set("grant_type", body.grant_type);
58:     if (typeof body?.scope === "string") params.set("scope", body.scope);
59:     if (typeof body?.resource === "string") params.append("resource", body.resource);
60:     if (Array.isArray(body?.resource)) {
61:       for (const resource of body.resource) {
62:         if (typeof resource === "string") params.append("resource", resource);
63:       }
64:     }
65:     return params;
66:   }
67: 
68:   return new URLSearchParams();
69: }
70: 
71: function invalidResourceResponse() {
72:   return new Response(
73:     JSON.stringify({
74:       error: "invalid_target",
75:       error_description: "The api:read scope requires a resource indicator.",
76:     }),
77:     { headers: { "content-type": "application/json" }, status: 400 },
78:   );
79: }

224: async function consumeRateLimit(
225:   database: D1Database,
226:   key: string,
227:   rule: { max: number; window: number },
228: ) {
229:   const now = Date.now();
230:   const windowMilliseconds = rule.window * 1000;
231:   const bucket = await database
232:     .prepare(
233:       `INSERT INTO rate_limit_buckets
234:         (bucket_key, window_started_at, count, updated_at)
235:        VALUES (?, ?, 1, ?)
236:        ON CONFLICT(bucket_key) DO UPDATE SET
237:          count = CASE
238:            WHEN rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at + ? <= ? THEN 1
239:            ELSE rate_limit_buckets.count + 1
240:          END,
241:          window_started_at = CASE
242:            WHEN rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at + ? <= ? THEN ?
243:            ELSE rate_limit_buckets.window_started_at
244:          END,
245:          updated_at = ?
246:        RETURNING count, window_started_at`,
247:     )
248:     .bind(key, now, now, windowMilliseconds, now, windowMilliseconds, now, now, now)
249:     .first<{ count: number; window_started_at: number }>();
250: 
251:   if (!bucket) return { allowed: false, retryAfter: rule.window };
252: 
253:   if (bucket.count === 1) {
254:     const db = createDb(database);
255:     await db
256:       .delete(rateLimitBuckets)
257:       .where(lt(rateLimitBuckets.updatedAt, now - 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000))
258:       .run();
259:   }
260: 
261:   const retryAfter = Math.max(
262:     0,
263:     Math.ceil((bucket.window_started_at + windowMilliseconds - now) / 1000),
264:   );
265: 
266:   return {
267:     allowed: bucket.count <= rule.max,
268:     retryAfter,
269:   };
270: }

17: export class M1ClientError extends Error {
18:   constructor(
19:     message: string,
20:     readonly status: number,
21:   ) {
22:     super(message);
23:     this.name = "M1ClientError";
24:   }

27: export async function m1Fetch<T>(path: string, init: RequestInit = {}) {
28:   const headers = new Headers(init.headers);
29:   if (init.body && !headers.has("content-type")) {
30:     headers.set("content-type", "application/json");
31:   }
32: 
33:   const response = await fetch(`/api${path}`, {
34:     ...init,
35:     headers,
36:   });
37:   const body = (await response.json().catch(() => null)) as { error?: string } | T | null;
38: 
39:   if (!response.ok) {
40:     throw new M1ClientError(readErrorMessage(body), response.status);
41:   }
42: 
43:   return body as T;
44: }

46: export async function reserveBootstrap(body: BootstrapTokenBody) {
47:   return unwrapTreatyResponse(await getTreaty().setup.reserve.post(body));
48: }

50: export async function completeBootstrap(body: BootstrapCompleteBody) {
51:   return unwrapTreatyResponse(await getTreaty().setup.complete.post(body));
52: }

54: export async function createInvitation(body: InvitationCreateBody) {
55:   return unwrapTreatyResponse(await getTreaty().invitations.post(body));
56: }

59:   return unwrapTreatyResponse(await getTreaty().invitations({ token }).get());
60: }

63:   return unwrapTreatyResponse(await getTreaty().invitations({ token }).accept.post(body));
64: }

66: function unwrapTreatyResponse<T>(result: { data: T | null; error: unknown; status: number }) {
67:   if (result.error) {
68:     const value =
69:       result.error && typeof result.error === "object" && "value" in result.error
70:         ? result.error.value
71:         : result.error;
72:     throw new M1ClientError(readErrorMessage(value), result.status);
73:   }
74: 
75:   if (result.data === null) {
76:     throw new M1ClientError("The request could not be completed.", result.status);
77:   }
78: 
79:   return result.data;
80: }
81: 
82: function readErrorMessage(value: unknown) {
83:   if (value && typeof value === "object" && "error" in value && typeof value.error === "string") {
84:     return value.error;
85:   }
86: 
87:   return "The request could not be completed.";
88: }

90: export function safeRedirect(value: string | undefined, fallback = "/") {
91:   if (!value || !value.startsWith("/") || value.startsWith("//")) return fallback;
92:   return value;

96:   if (error instanceof M1ClientError && error.status === 429) {
97:     return "Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.";
98:   }
99:

52: async function sha256Base64Url(value: string) {
53:   const digest = new Uint8Array(
54:     await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", new TextEncoder().encode(value)),
55:   );
56:   let binary = "";
57:   for (const byte of digest) binary += String.fromCharCode(byte);
58: 
59:   return btoa(binary).replaceAll("+", "-").replaceAll("/", "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
60: }

236:     state,
237:   });
238:   const response = await SELF.fetch(`${origin}/api/auth/oauth2/authorize?${params}`, {
239:     headers: { cookie },
240:     redirect: "manual",
241:   });
242:   const location = response.headers.get("location");

244:   expect(response.status).toBe(302);

247:   const callback = new URL(location ?? redirectUri);
